rules:
<number_rules>
A reader must be able to check where every quantity on this page comes from. So every quantity you write is a token, however you
would otherwise write it: in digits, as a number word ("three years"), a fraction ("a third"), a range, a rate or a multiplier
("twice"). Python prints the value with its qualifier (a rate with its per part); write the unit after the token ("[[<id>]] days")
when what it prints, in <registry> or <mentions>, shows none.
- A figure the data holds as a number: its id from <registry>.
- A quantity the records' text, the brief or the announcement states: its id from <mentions>. Python prints it as the source writes
  it, "about" and "up to" included. A quantity the list does not hold: [[q:<where>|<the words exactly as the text writes them>]],
  <where> being <endpoint>.<record id>.<field> (<endpoint>.<field> when the endpoint is itself the record), brief or announcement.
- A comparison of two figures: [[calc:<op>|<id a>|<id b>]], <op> being diff (a − b), pct_of (a as a percent of b), pct_less or
  pct_more (how far a is below or above b, as a percent of b), times (a ÷ b) or pp (the gap between two shares, printed as points).
  Python computes it. Each of <id a> and <id b> is an id from <registry> or a mention that prints a plain number — never a number
  of your own, a range, a ratio, a bound or a figure with a qualifier ("about", "up to"): Python refuses those, and the sentence goes.
  diff and pp join figures of the same people, place and period; a comparison false as named is removed.
- Where you say how many items a list holds, write [[count:<list>]], <list> being the list's field name in a reply's schema
  (kpis, risks, phases, judge_qa, …): Python prints how many items the page shows.
- A number of your own — a target, a threshold, a duration, a staffing level, a count in the program's own design (one named contact
  per landlord): [[model:<number>|<what it is>]], a number and never a range (each end of a range is its own proposal). It shows as your assumption; a share is written as a percent ("[[model:3%|…]]").
- A field the reply's schema types as a number (a count, a percent, a day, a target) holds a plain number, never a token: tokens go in
  text.
- A name that has digits and is no quantity: write a year, a date, a time, an age after the word "age" and the data's own names
  plainly; anything else as [[nf:<the text>|<kind>]], <kind> being age, year, date, time, name, code or phone.
- A name you write — a staff role's title, an outcome's category — holds no quantity: the number goes in the field that holds it
  (count, rate, duration_years) or in your prose.
- If none of these fits, write the sentence without the quantity and say what is not known. A quantity in another spelling is
  counted as having no link; a token that names nothing (a wrong id, a form with a part missing) takes its sentence off the page.
</number_rules>
<examples>
1. A duration of your own, such as the target time to a first placement: [[model:3|weeks from intake to a first placement]] weeks.
2. A figure the text states with its own qualifier: [[q.84d8e]] — cite the id; Python prints the source's words, qualifier included.
3. A comparison Python computes: [[calc:pct_of|status001-reachable|status001-total]].
4. A code with digits that counts nothing: [[nf:Form W-9|code]].
5. How many items a list holds: [[count:calendar]] — Python prints how many items the page shows.
</examples>
